acceptance.check: A member records a payment choosing from, to, amount and optional note, in full or in part, and both balances move by exactly that amount without a page reload.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Seed a group with a 10.00 debt, record a 4.00 payment in the balances-screen form, assert both nets moved by 4.00 and the page did not navigate.

acceptance.check: A recorded payment appears in the group activity naming who recorded it, when, and between whom and for how much.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Record a payment then read the group's activity; assert one payment.recorded entry with actor, timestamp, from/to and string amountMinor.

acceptance.check: A partial payment leaves the remainder owed: per-member table shows it and the transfer list is recomputed from the new balances.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Record a partial payment; assert the member table figures and that simplifyDebts over the new nets equals the rendered transfer list.

acceptance.check: Either involved member can delete a payment after confirming in a dialog that names it and both balances return exactly; a third member is refused.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Delete as the recipient, confirm the named dialog, assert nets restored; attempt delete as a third member and assert refusal with nothing written.

acceptance.check: Payment write and its activity entry commit in one transaction: a failed write leaves no entry and a success leaves exactly one.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run tests/integration/payments.test.ts atomicity cases (recordActivity mock throw, then success count).

acceptance.check: Non-member parties and non-positive amounts are refused with the reason beside the field and the form keeps every typed value.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Submit unknown member and zero amount; assert field errors adjacent to from/to/amount and all inputs retain their values and focus moves to the first invalid field.

acceptance.check: The submit button disables and reads 'Recording…' while the write is in flight and is the only busy state.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Slow the action, click Record payment, assert the button shows 'Recording…' and is disabled; assert no other spinner or skeleton appears for the submit.

alternatives_considered.approach: Model payments as negative expenses (payer/share rows on a zero-total expense) to reuse the expense write path.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would smuggle payments through expense_payer/expense_share, breaking TR-4's readable invariant that balances sum stored expense rows plus stored payment rows and that expense edits never touch payments; a dedicated table keeps the two ledgers independently auditable and the activity kinds distinct.

alternatives_considered.approach: Host the delete control on the activity feed entry instead of a Payments section on the balances screen.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Feed screens are explicitly out of scope for this piece, so the delete would land in code this ticket does not own; the balances screen already owns settle-up and can list payments newest-first with the same dialog pattern as DeleteExpenseButton.

validated_work_order.approach: Add a payments table per TRD (id, group_id, from_member_id, to_member_id, amount_minor bigint, note, recorded_by, created_at, deleted_at with soft-delete) plus payment.recorded/payment.deleted activity kinds and a 'payment' subject type. Define the payment's balance effect as from += amount and to -= amount (debtor pays creditor: e.g. Sam at -10.00 paying Priya 10.00 leaves Sam 0 and Priya 10.00 less owed), which preserves the zero-sum invariant simplifyDebts asserts. Extend readNetByMember with two payment sums (outgoing by from_member_id, incoming by to_member_id, both filtered to group_id, deleted_at null, and the memberOfGroup predicate) so net = paid - shared + (sumFrom - sumTo); extend listGroupsForUser with the same adjustment keyed by the caller's own membership row so home totals stay the sum of per-group balances (TR-8). Add access helpers createPayment (insert-select-where memberOfGroup guard), softDeletePayment (guarded UPDATE setting deleted_at, authorised by caller memberId being from or to), and readPaymentsForGroup (newest first with resolved names, null for non-members). Add src/app/actions/payments.ts with recordPayment and deletePayment following the expenses.ts/members.ts shape: Zod parse in-file, requireUser, single db.transaction writing payment row plus exactly one recordActivity entry, typed { ok, fieldErrors, formError } result, revalidatePath('/', 'layout'), no redirect inside the transaction, money parsed/formatted only via src/lib/money.ts (parseMajorUnits/formatMinor) with the same MAX_INT8 bound. Validation: both members active in the group, from != to, amount positive and in group currency, note <= 500 chars, archived group refused, invalid choice refused beside its field with typed values kept (controlled inputs). Delete: caller must be an active member AND one of the two involved members; third member refused; double-delete answers success with no second entry (guarded UPDATE on deleted_at is null). UI: new client PaymentForm (from/to selects defaulting to the first simplified transfer's ends when present, amount with fixed currency symbol, optional note, field errors beside fields, submit Button busyLabel 'Recording…' as the only busy state, on success router.refresh() so balances and transfer list update without navigation or reload) and DeletePaymentButton (Dialog titled with the concrete payment, e.g. 'Delete payment of €10.00 from Sam to Priya?', consequence 'Both balances return to what they were before this payment.', destructive confirm). BalancesScreen renders a 'Payments' list (newest first, Money with direction words, note, per-row delete control for involved members) above/after the transfer Card and replaces the disabled placeholder with PaymentForm; balances page fetches payments and passes them in. Migration via drizzle-kit generate (drizzle/0004) applied by the existing boot migrator on both drivers.
assumptions: Group currency is fixed at creation and every payment amount is parsed in it via parseMajorUnits; no per-payment currency field (TRD payment entity lists none).
from/to selects default to the first simplified transfer's debtor/creditor when one exists, else the first two canonical members; any active member pair remains valid.
MAX_INT8 bound (9223372036854775807n) applies to payment amounts exactly as to expense amounts, refused beside the amount field.
Delete authorisation requires the caller to be currently active AND one of the two members; a logged-out or removed caller gets the same 404/unavailable answer as other group writes.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: The load-bearing claims were re-checked directly against the code and docs: no payments table or payment activity kinds in src/db/schema.ts, the disabled Record payment placeholder in balances-screen.tsx, the two balance-sum sites in src/lib/access.ts, the TRD payment entity with deleted_at backing soft-delete, and docs/ui.md already describing the Record payment form shape so no approved-doc edit is needed. The remaining uncertainty is judgment calls (payment-list placement, double-delete idempotency), each flagged in risks or residual_risks with TRD backing.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: The critique file was empty ({}), so there were no findings to judge and nothing contradicting the binding decisions in plan/brief.md to dismiss. I therefore verified the proposal's key claims myself against the code and docs rather than adjudicating a debate: the missing-table/missing-kinds/missing-action diagnosis is correct, the two balance-sum sites are as described, the soft-delete choice is backed by the TRD payment entity's deleted_at column, and all seven IAC items have test-or-browser coverage. I kept the proposal's approach intact and made the residual risks explicit instead of leaving that list empty.

qa_script: Seed the app and open /groups/[id]/balances for a group with a known debt (e.g. Sam owes Priya €10.00).
Choose from Sam to Priya, amount 4.00, note 'first part', submit; confirm both nets moved by €4.00 and the transfer list now shows €6.00 remaining without a reload.
Open the group activity; confirm one entry naming the recorder, Sam, Priya and €4.00 with a time.
Submit amount 0 and an unknown member; confirm field-level errors beside amount/from and that all typed values remain.
Click delete on the €4.00 payment; confirm the dialog names '€4.00 from Sam to Priya' with a destructive confirm; confirm and check both balances returned exactly.
As a third member, attempt the same delete (via the payment id); confirm refusal and unchanged balances.
residual_risks: Double-delete answers success with no second entry rather than 404; QA should confirm the second delete leaves balances and the feed untouched.
Soft-deleted rows remain in the payments table for the feed entry to reference; a future export or audit view must remember to filter deleted_at, or deleted payments will reappear there.

Payment-list placement on the balances screen is an interpretation of docs/ui.md (which names only the Record payment action there); QA should confirm it does not crowd the transfer list that is the screen's answer.
risks: Payment-history placement is an interpretation: docs/ui.md Balances Regions lists only table, transfer list and Record payment action, but the delete control needs a row to live on while feed screens (piece 8) are out of scope, so this plan adds a Payments section to the balances screen rather than the feed.

Soft-delete vs hard-delete: TRD gives payment a deleted_at column, so this plan soft-deletes (balance reads filter it) even though the issue says 'removes the row'; the visible effect is identical but the row remains for the feed entry to reference.

From/to must be active members; a placeholder is allowed while active. An involved member who has since left cannot delete until rejoining (TR-1 non-members see 404), which the plan states rather than silently permitting.
No docs/ or .sdlc/ changes: docs/ui.md already describes the Record payment form shape and TR-4/TR-7 already state the rewritten invariant, so no approved-doc edit is proposed.

validated_work_order.understanding: Settle-up payments do not exist yet: there is no payments table (src/db/schema.ts has users/sessions/groups/members/expenses/expense_payer/expense_share/expense_split_input/activity/login_attempts only), no src/app/actions/payments.ts, and BalancesScreen renders a disabled 'Record payment' placeholder. Balances are read in exactly two places that must both change: src/lib/access.ts readNetByMember (used by readMembers, readBalancesForGroup, readNetBalanceForMember, hence by the balances page, group overview, members screen and leave/remove guards) which sums expense_payer minus expense_share only, and listGroupsForUser which repeats the same two sums inline for the home totals. Callers of readBalancesForGroup are src/app/(app)/page.tsx, src/app/(app)/groups/[id]/page.tsx and src/app/(app)/groups/[id]/balances/page.tsx. Activity kinds are expense/member/group only; there is no payment.recorded/deleted kind and activitySubjectTypes is ['expense'] only. The binding decisions are already in the code: split rule stored in expense_split_input, balances read only from payer/share rows, and TR-4's rewrite (edit/delete replaces stored rows in one transaction with the activity entry; split-algorithm changes never restate history). This plan extends that rule to payments: a payment is stored rows plus exactly one activity entry in one transaction, and balances sum stored expense rows plus stored payment rows, never a re-evaluation.
unknowns: Whether QA seed (piece 9, TR-26) should include a sample payment; this plan does not change the seed endpoint, only notes a payment fixture would help IAC coverage.
